name: Prepositional-phrase attachment
description: A small English fragment where a prepositional phrase can modify either a noun phrase (NP -> NP PP) or a verb phrase (VP -> VP PP). Both rules are left-recursive. Each extra PP multiplies the readings: 1 PP gives 2 parses, 2 PPs give 5, 3 PPs give 14 (Catalan numbers).
grammar:
# An educational fragment of English, not a grammar of the language.
S       -> NP VP
NP      -> Pronoun | Det N | NP PP
VP      -> V NP | VP PP
PP      -> P NP
Pronoun -> "I" | "she"
Det     -> "the" | "a"
N       -> "man" | "telescope" | "hill" | "park" | "student" | "book"
V       -> "saw" | "reads"
P       -> "with" | "on" | "in"

examples.text: I saw the man with a telescope
examples.note: Two readings. Who has the telescope?

examples.text: She saw the man on the hill with a telescope
